headline: Bluesky has expanded Attie, its AI app, so that anyone can build websites, quizzes, games and polls for their own communities.
score_reason: Confirmed by Bluesky's chief executive at an event; early, experimental product whose uptake is unknown.
importance_line: Ordinary users, not just programmers, can build small interactive things for friends and groups on Bluesky's network, which could help the network win back users, though its engagement has been falling.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Bluesky announced at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Thursday an expansion of Attie, its experimental AI app that first built custom feeds, so users can create websites, quizzes, games and polls that live on the AT Protocol, the open standard behind Bluesky. Toni Schneider, Bluesky's chief executive and a former chief executive of Automattic, called it "vibe coding for your community", where users bring their own AI model or use open-weight ones; Bluesky has 47 million registered users, but engagement has declined.
